text:
Camila Reyes: Kicking off the regulated workloads vertical ABM pilot planning here (FinServ + Healthcare). Goal: 6–8 week pilot, ship a tight asset set + run coordinated outbound. Dropping owners + timeline draft—please reply w/ gaps + dependencies.

Camila Reyes: Week 0–1 (this + next week):
- ICP/personas + messaging framework (PMM) 
- Target list sanity check w/ Sales (we’ll do async)
- Success metrics + tracking plan (Growth + MOPs)
- Draft outbound sequences (PMM + Content)

Camila Reyes: Week 2–3:
- Landing pages (FinServ + Healthcare) + forms (Growth + Design + Eng)
- Vertical pitch deck v1 (PMM + SE)
- Security FAQ addendum per vertical (Security/GRC + PMM)
- Private/VPC reference architecture (SE + Private)

Camila Reyes: Week 3–6:
- Outbound launch + iterate weekly
- 1 webinar/roundtable (Events)
- Partner intro motion (light) 

Camila Reyes: Week 6–8:
- Push advanced accounts through security/procurement
- Retro + decide if we scale to more verticals

Camila Reyes: Asset list we’re committing to (small but high-quality):
1) Landing pages (FS + HC)
2) Pitch deck (FS + HC)
3) Security/compliance FAQ addendum (FS + HC)
4) Private/VPC reference architecture diagram + “who owns what” table

Camila Reyes: Hard dependency callout: Security/GRC review needs to be early + fast so we don’t ship risky claims. @Dr. Aisha Rahman @Olga Petrov can we align on review SLAs + what evidence we can share w/o NDA?

Soojin Lee: PMM owning messaging + decks. I’ll post a v0 narrative + “approved phrasing / do-not-say” list by EOD tomorrow. Biggest risk is retention/residency wording + on-prem maturity, so I’ll keep it conservative.

Ben Carter: Growth can own landing pages + tracking. Need: 1) final CTA, 2) what form fields are required for routing, 3) UTM conventions. @Tyler Benson let’s sync on HubSpot fields + dedupe rules.

Tyler Benson: Yep. For routing, we can do: vertical=FS/HC + deployment_interest=Hosted/Dedicated/Private + “Security review requested” checkbox. Also capture company domain, country/region, and “regulated data type” (PHI/PCI/PII/other). Dedupe on email + domain.

Ethan Wallace: Content here. I can draft the landing page copy + outbound email sequence copy in parallel. Need firm guidance on what we can/can’t promise re: SOC2, audit log retention, and prompt storage.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: We can commit to a 48-hour turnaround for copy review *if* we’re reviewing in one doc w/ tracked changes and the ask is clearly marked (what claim, where it’s going, audience). Evidence sharing: SOC 2 report only under NDA, but we can share an “attestation summary” and high-level control statements publicly.

Olga Petrov: +1. Please avoid absolute statements like “we never store X” unless we specify deployment mode and config. We should stick to: what’s logged by default, configurable retention, and boundaries between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Soojin Lee: Great. I’ll create a “security safe words” section in the messaging doc and link to the FAQ addenda. Also, we should add a standard footnote: “capabilities vary by deployment mode; details in security review.”

Markus Klein: SE can own the “reference architecture + responsibilities” and sanity-check decks. We should make sure Private/VPC diagram shows: customer VPC boundary, logging to customer SIEM, KMS/HSM integration points, and what Redwood control plane touches.

Simran Kaur: I can do the diagram + a 1-pager explaining networking assumptions (peering vs private link), DNS/TLS, egress allowlists. If we can get a design resource for polish, even better.

Noura El-Khoury: Events can do a small roundtable instead of a big webinar if we want higher intent. If we do webinar: need speakers + abstract + landing page by end of Week 2 for promotion.

Camila Reyes: Love the roundtable idea. Let’s decide format by Friday based on list quality + partner availability.

Ben Carter: For landing pages, can we align on CTA? My vote: “Book a 30-min Private/VPC architecture review” + secondary “Request security FAQ”. Keeps intent high.

Soojin Lee: Agree. For HC, maybe “Schedule PHI-safe deployment consult” is too cute—might spook people. Keep it plain.

Sofia Mendes: Looping in legal hat: if we say “PHI-safe” we should be prepared for “are you signing a BAA?” questions. Recommend: “Deploy LLM inference for PHI workflows with Private/VPC options” and then handle BAA in sales/security process.

Ethan Wallace: Noted. I’ll avoid “HIPAA compliant by default” and stick to “supports HIPAA-aligned controls depending on deployment + customer configuration.”

Tyler Benson: Re HubSpot: I can set up a dedicated campaign + list membership rules for the pilot. Need naming convention: “ABM-Regulated-2024Q1-FS” / “ABM-Regulated-2024Q1-HC”.

Camila Reyes: Works. @Tyler Benson please also add Slack notifications for high-intent form fills (Private + Security review). Route to #sales + #solutions-eng maybe.

Tyler Benson: Can do. We’ll send a concise alert: name, company, vertical, region, notes, UTM source, and suggested owner.

Markus Klein: On the deck: please include a slide that clearly distinguishes Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and what changes for auditability + data boundaries. Prospects ask this in minute 5.

Soojin Lee: Yep. I’ll make that the “deployment decision tree” slide for both decks.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Security FAQ addenda: I want a single template w/ variable sections per vertical so we’re not maintaining two totally separate documents. Olga + I can draft the base this week.

Olga Petrov: I’ll add a “questionnaire-ready” section (short answers) and a “talk track” section (how to explain in a call). Also: explicit language around audit log export formats + retention options.

Ben Carter: Metrics: I’ll draft a simple dashboard spec: engagement → meetings → POC scoped → security review started → procurement steps. We should define what counts as “security review started” (e.g., questionnaire received vs call booked).

Camila Reyes: Define “started” as (1) questionnaire received OR (2) security review call scheduled w/ security attendee. We can refine later.

Ethan Wallace: For outbound sequence copy: I’ll need persona split. Are we doing CISO/GRC + Platform Eng + ML Eng tracks?

Soojin Lee: Yes, but keep it minimal: 2 tracks to start.
- Track A: Security/GRC (risk + audit + residency + retention)
- Track B: Platform/ML (latency/cost predictability + deployment flexibility + observability)

Camila Reyes: +1. Also please keep the subject lines conservative. No “HIPAA-ready in 2 weeks” stuff.

Ben Carter: Timeline risk: landing page form routing depends on Eng. Are we staffed?

Camila Reyes: I’m flagging to Product/Eng separately, but in the meantime let’s structure the page so we can launch copy w/ a simple “book a meeting” link if routing slips.

Simran Kaur: For reference architecture: I can deliver a “good enough” diagram by end of Week 2, then iterate. Need confirmation on what’s GA vs beta for Private installer pieces.

Markus Klein: I’ll ping Vivek (Private owner) for GA/beta boundaries and post here.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Another dependency: we need to align on what we say about audit logging “token-level” vs “request-level.” Marketing claims have drifted in the past.

Soojin Lee: Good call. I’ll add a line in the messaging doc: “audit logs cover API request metadata and admin actions; token-level traces are available in the console for authorized users” (if accurate). Markus/Aisha please correct me if not.

Markus Klein: That’s mostly right. We should not imply we log raw prompts/outputs in audit logs. Those are separate from application logs.

Olga Petrov: Please explicitly say: “Audit logs do not include customer content by default.” If a customer chooses to enable additional logging in their environment, that’s on them.

Ethan Wallace: Got it. I’ll draft copy w/ “by default” qualifiers + deployment mode callouts.

Noura El-Khoury: For the roundtable/webinar: tentative title draft: “Running LLM inference for regulated data: latency, cost, and auditability without vendor lock-in.” Thoughts?

Camila Reyes: Works. Keep it pragmatic and avoid “compliance theater” language.

Tyler Benson: FYI I can add a “security review requested” checkbox + trigger an auto-email w/ links to the public security overview + “what we can share under NDA” note.

Sofia Mendes: Please route that auto-email copy through me + Aisha first. Anything that looks like we’re offering to share SOC2 without NDA will create problems.

Camila Reyes: Action items recap (reply w/ objections):
- @Soojin Lee messaging framework v0 + approved phrasing list by tomorrow EOD
- @Ethan Wallace draft landing page copy + 2 outbound sequences by Monday
- @Ben Carter landing page wire + metrics spec by Tuesday
- @Tyler Benson HubSpot fields + routing + Slack alerts proposal by Tuesday
- @Dr. Aisha Rahman / @Olga Petrov security FAQ base template + review SLA confirmed (48h) by this week
- @Simran Kaur reference architecture diagram v0 by end of Week 2
- @Noura El-Khoury propose roundtable run-of-show + speakers by Friday

Camila Reyes: We’ll do a 30-min ABM pilot standup weekly. I’ll send a calendar hold.

Slackbot: Reminder: Camila Reyes set a reminder for this thread.

Ben Carter: :thumbsup: No objections. One more: please ensure we have a “request a security review” path that doesn’t require a full sales meeting (some CISOs want docs first). We can still route to SE after.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: That’s fine as long as it’s the “public security overview + NDA gate for SOC2 report.” We can do a short security triage call if they want.

Soojin Lee: I’ll make sure CTA options include: (1) book architecture review, (2) request security package.

Camila Reyes: Perfect. Keep updates in this thread as you ship drafts/links. :rocket:
